question: Who among the following appoints the members of the State Public Service Commission (SPSC) under Article 316 of the Constitution of India? (RRB Technician Grade III (10/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: President of India
Chief Justice of the High Court
Prime Minister of India
Governor of the State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor of the State

Explanation:
According to Article 316 of the Indian Constitution, the Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commission (SPSC) are appointed by the Governor of the State. The Governor follows the procedure laid down by the Constitution while making these appointments. The term of office for members is 6 years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier. The Governor can recommend the removal of members, but the final authority for removal lies with the President. The primary function of SPSC is to conduct recruitment for state civil services.

☛ Article 316 deals with? → Appointment and term of SPSC members
☛ What is the term of a SPSC member? → 6 years or age 62
☛ Who has the power to remove SPSC members? → President (on Governor's recommendation)
☛ Main function of SPSC? → Recruitment for state civil services

question: How many Fundamental Duties were originally added to the Indian Constitution in 1976? (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: 8
10
9
12
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 10

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, under Part IV-A, Article 51A. Originally, 10 duties were included. Later, in 2002, the 86th Amendment added one more duty, making the total count 11. These duties remind citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation. The concept of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the Soviet Union. They were incorporated on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts.

☛ Which committee recommended Fundamental Duties? → Swaran Singh Committee

question: Which Article allows the President to recommend President’s Rule in a state? (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Article 356
Article 353
Article 245
Article 360
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 356

Explanation:
Article 356 empowers the President to impose President's Rule in a state when the constitutional machinery fails. This is also known as 'State Emergency' or 'Constitutional Emergency'. It falls under Part XVIII (Emergency Provisions) of the Indian Constitution. During President's Rule, the state government is suspended, and the administration is taken over by the central government. Initially, it remains in force for six months and can be extended up to three years with parliamentary approval every six months. Article 353 deals with National Emergency, Article 245 with center-state legislative relations, and Article 360 with Financial Emergency.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article related to President's Rule → Article 356
☛ When is President's Rule imposed? → When the state government fails to function according to the Constitution
☛ Maximum duration of President's Rule → 3 years (requires parliamentary approval every 6 months)
☛ Part containing President's Rule → Part XVIII (Emergency Provisions)
☛ Legislative authority during President's Rule → Parliament
question_hi: कौन-सा अनुच्छेद, राष्ट्रपति को किसी राज्य में राष्ट्रपति शासन की अनुशंसा करने का अधिकार देता है? (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 3)

Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 356

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 356 के तहत राष्ट्रपति को किसी राज्य में संवैधानिक तंत्र के विफल होने पर राष्ट्रपति शासन लागू करने की शक्ति प्राप्त है। इसे 'राष्ट्रपति शासन' या 'संवैधानिक आपातकाल' भी कहा जाता है। यह प्रावधान संविधान के भाग XVIII (आपातकालीन प्रावधान) में आता है। राष्ट्रपति शासन लागू होने पर राज्य सरकार को निलंबित कर दिया जाता है और राज्य का प्रशासन केंद्र सरकार के नियंत्रण में आ जाता है। यह प्रारंभ में 6 महीने के लिए लागू होता है और संसद की स्वीकृति से अधिकतम 3 वर्ष तक बढ़ाया जा सकता है। अनुच्छेद 353 राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल, अनुच्छेद 245 केंद्र-राज्य विधायी संबंध, और अनुच्छेद 360 वित्तीय आपातकाल से संबंधित है।

question: The governor’s power to issue ordinances is mentioned in which Article of the Indian Constitution? (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: 112
199
123
213
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 213

Explanation:
Article 213 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Governor to issue ordinances. This power is exercised when the state legislature is not in session and immediate action is required. An ordinance has the same force as a legislative act but ceases to operate six weeks after the legislature reassembles unless approved. This differs from Article 123, which grants similar powers to the President at the national level. The Governor's ordinance-making power is part of Part VI of the Constitution, dealing with state executive. It is a discretionary power but must follow constitutional limitations.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article for Governor's ordinance power → 213
☛ Article for President's ordinance power → 123
☛ When can Governor issue ordinance? → When legislature not in session
☛ Maximum duration of ordinance → 6 weeks after session starts
☛ Ordinance has same effect as → an Act of legislature

question:

(RRB NTPC Tier I (09/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: Prime Minister
President of India
Chief Justice of India
Speaker of Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Speaker of Lok Sabha

Explanation:
The Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) in India is a parliamentary committee that examines the functioning of public sector undertakings (PSUs). The chairperson of COPU is appointed by the Speaker of Lok Sabha. The appointment is made from among the members of Lok Sabha, and the chairperson is usually a member of the opposition. question: Which of the following British Indian government legislations provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta, comprising one chief justice and three other judges? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Amending Act of 1781
Regulating Act of 1773
Pitt’s India Act of 1784
Charter Act of 1793
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Regulating Act of 1773

Explanation:
The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first legislation passed by the British Parliament to regulate the administration of the East India Company in India. This act provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta, consisting of one chief justice and three other judges. The court had jurisdiction over civil, criminal, and admiralty matters in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. Additionally, the act laid down the foundation for the British government's control over the Company's affairs. It also appointed Warren Hastings as the first Governor-General of Bengal.

question: Which of the following British Indian government legislation separated for the first time 'provincial budgets' from the 'central budget' and authorised the provincial legislatures to enact their budgets? (RRB Paramedical (13/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Government of India Act of 1935
Indian Councils Act of 1892
Indian Councils Act of 1909
Government of India Act of 1919
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act of 1919

Explanation:
The Government of India Act of 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, for the first time separated provincial budgets from the central budget. It empowered provincial legislatures to prepare and pass their own budgets, promoting decentralization of financial powers. Before this act, all budgets were controlled by the central government. This act introduced dyarchy (dual government), dividing provincial subjects into transferred and reserved categories. It gave provinces financial autonomy, allowing them to allocate resources according to local needs. This was a significant step towards federalism in British India.

question: Which of the following Directive Principles was NOT added to the Indian Constitution as part of the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 1)

Article 38: State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities
Article 39: To secure opportunities for healthy development of children
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 38

Explanation:
The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added four new Directive Principles to the Constitution: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (participation of workers in management of industries), Article 48A (protection of environment and wildlife), and Article 43 (development of libraries). It also added clause (f) to Article 39 to secure opportunities for healthy development of children. Article 38 was originally part of the Constitution; the 42nd Amendment only added a directive to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities alongside social, economic and political justice. Thus, Article 38 was not a new addition but an amendment.

question: Which of the following amendments to the Indian Constitution is regarded as a major milestone in the country’s taxation system for introducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST)? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: 97th Amendment, 2011
101st Amendment, 2016
100th Amendment, 2015
86th Amendment, 2002
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 101st Amendment, 2016

Explanation:
The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 is considered a major milestone in India's taxation system as it introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST). This amendment enabled both the Centre and States to levy tax simultaneously, creating a unified tax structure across the country. It provided for the formation of the GST Council, comprising the Union Finance Minister and State Finance Ministers, to recommend rates and rules. The amendment replaced multiple indirect taxes like service tax, VAT, excise duty, etc. with a single GST. The reform came into effect on July 1, 2017, and is famously known as 'One Nation, One Tax'.

question: Division of legislative subjects into union, state and concurrent List is contained in which of the following schedules of the Constitution of India? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 1)

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the division of legislative subjects into three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. The Union List originally had 97 subjects, now 100, on which only Parliament can legislate. The State List originally 66, now 61 subjects, on which state legislatures can legislate. question: Which of the following is NOT one of the valid ways to acquire Indian citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: By registration
By marriage
By birth
By descent
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is By marriage

Explanation:
Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, there are five ways to acquire Indian citizenship: by birth, by descent, by registration, by naturalization, and by incorporation of territory. Marriage is not a direct mode of acquiring citizenship. A foreign woman marrying an Indian citizen may apply for citizenship through registration or naturalization, but marriage alone does not confer citizenship. Citizenship by birth is granted to persons born in India on or after January 26, 1950 (with some exceptions). Citizenship by descent is for children born outside India to Indian parents. Registration is available for certain categories like persons of Indian origin. Naturalization involves a formal process for foreigners. Incorporation of territory occurs when new land becomes part of India.

question: The provision of 'Single citizenship' for all in the Indian Constitution is adopted from the constitution of which of the following countries? (RRB Technician Grade III (10/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: US Constitution
British Constitution
Australian Constitution
Canadian Constitution
solution:

Explanation:
The concept of single citizenship in the Indian Constitution is adopted from the British Constitution. It means that every person in India enjoys only one citizenship, that of the Union, promoting unity and integrity. Unlike the United States, which has a system of dual citizenship (federal and state), India follows the British model. The provisions related to citizenship are detailed in Part II (Articles 5 to 11) of the Indian Constitution. This adoption helped in preventing regionalism and fostering a sense of national identity. The British system also influenced India's parliamentary system and legislative process.

question: The Constitution of India provided for how many types of emergencies in Part XVIII, from Articles 352 to 360? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Three
Four
Six
Five
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Three

Explanation:
Part XVIII (Articles 352 to 360) of the Indian Constitution provides for three types of emergencies: National Emergency (Article 352), Failure of Constitutional Machinery in States or President's Rule (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360). National Emergency is proclaimed on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. President's Rule is imposed when a state's constitutional machinery fails. Financial Emergency is declared when India's financial stability or credit is threatened. During these emergencies, fundamental rights are affected. The President has the power to proclaim these emergencies, and they require parliamentary approval.

question: The term 'Armed Rebellion' was introduced under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution for the proclamation of a National Emergency by which Constitutional Amendment? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002
61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988
44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978

Explanation:
Originally, Article 352 used the term 'internal disturbance' for proclamation of National Emergency. The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced it with 'armed rebellion' to prevent misuse. This amendment made it harder to impose emergency and added provisions for judicial review. Now, emergency can be declared only on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion, not internal disturbance. The change was recommended by the Swaran Singh Committee and enacted by the Morarji Desai government.

question: In India, which of the following is NOT considered as a constitutional body? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: National Human Rights Commission

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Human Rights Commission

Explanation:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is a statutory body, established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act. It is not created by the Constitution but by an act of Parliament. In contrast, the Election Commission of India (Article 324), Union Public Service Commission (Articles 315-323), and Finance Commission of India (Article 280) are constitutional bodies because they are directly mentioned in the Constitution, and their powers, composition, and functions are defined by it. NHRC is a statutory body formed by the government to protect human rights but does not have constitutional status.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) to safeguard the rights of the Scheduled Castes? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Article 330
Article 350
Article 338
Article 340
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 338

Explanation:
Article 338 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) to safeguard the rights of Scheduled Castes. The Commission consists of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and three other members appointed by the President. Its primary role is to monitor constitutional and legal safeguards, investigate complaints, and make recommendations to the government regarding the welfare of Scheduled Castes. Article 330 deals with reservation of seats for SCs/STs in the Lok Sabha, Article 350 with linguistic minorities, and Article 340 with the commission for backward classes. The NCSC was originally a single commission for both SCs and STs, but was later bifurcated by the 89th Amendment (2003) into separate commissions for SCs and STs.

question: Words 'Integrity', 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by which of the following amendments? (RRB Paramedical (13/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: 24th Amendment, 1971
42nd Amendment, 1976
44th Amendment, 1978
52nd Amendment, 1985
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Amendment, 1976

Explanation:
The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment (1976). This amendment was enacted during the Prime Ministership of Indira Gandhi and is often called the 'Mini-Constitution'. It also added Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A). In the Preamble, 'Socialist' implies equality and social justice; 'Secular' means religious neutrality; and 'Integrity' signifies national unity. These words reflect the core philosophy of India. The amendment also modified Article 368, which deals with the amendment process. It was a comprehensive amendment that changed many provisions of the Constitution.

question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India provides for the mechanism and power of Parliament to amend the Constitution? (RRB Technician Grade III (10/03/2026) Shift 3)

Article 356
Article 368
solution:

Explanation:

This article details the amendment procedure, which involves introducing a bill in either House of Parliament and passing it with a special majority. It protects the basic structure of the Constitution, as established by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case. question: Which of the following 1973 landmark judgments of the Supreme Court of India provided that Parliament cannot amend the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution through amendments? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Champakam Dorairanjan Case
Minerva Mills Case
Kesavananda Bharati Case
Golakhnath Case
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kesavananda Bharati Case

Explanation:
In the 1973 landmark case of Kesavananda Bharati, the Supreme Court of India ruled that Parliament cannot amend the basic structure of the Constitution. This doctrine limited the amending power of Parliament, protecting core principles like democracy, secularism, judicial review, and federalism. The decision was made by a 13-judge bench with a 7:6 majority. It overruled the Golakhnath Case (1967), which had held that fundamental rights could not be amended. The case was filed by a Kerala monastery, Kesavananda Bharati, and became a cornerstone in safeguarding the Constitution's integrity. The basic structure doctrine has since been reaffirmed in subsequent cases like Minerva Mills (1980) and Waman Rao (1981).

भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 47 राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों (DPSP) में शामिल है। यह अनुच्छेद राज्य को निर्देश देता है कि वह पोषण स्तर और सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य में सुधार करे तथा मादक पेय पदार्थों और स्वास्थ्य के लिए हानिकारक नशीली दवाओं के सेवन पर प्रतिबंध लगाए। यह राज्य को कृषि संगठन और पशुपालन को आधुनिक और वैज्ञानिक तरीकों से विकसित करने का भी निर्देश देता है। यह अनुच्छेद समाज कल्याण को बढ़ावा देने और नागरिकों के जीवन स्तर को ऊपर उठाने पर केंद्रित है। पर्यावरण संरक्षण अनुच्छेद 48-A में शामिल है।

question: Which of the following is not contained in Article 51? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Just and honourable relations between nations
Promotion of international peace and security
Protection of forests and wildlife of India
Respect for international law and treaty obligations
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Protection of forests and wildlife of India

Explanation:
Article 51 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution. This article promotes international peace and security, maintains just and honourable relations between nations, fosters respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourages settlement of international disputes by arbitration. It directs the State to endeavour to preserve international peace and security. The protection of forests and wildlife is covered under Article 48A, which deals with environmental protection, not Article 51. Hence, option 3 is not contained in Article 51.

question: Right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years is provided under which Article? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Article 51A(k)
Article 45
Article 21A
Article 19
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21A

Explanation:
Article 21A of the Indian Constitution provides the right to free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years. This article was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. To implement this right, the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (RTE Act) was enacted. Earlier, Article 45 (now a Directive Principle) provided for education for children up to 14 years, but it was not a fundamental right. With Article 21A, education became a fundamental right, making it enforceable by law. Article 51A(k) mentions the duty of parents to provide education to their children aged 6-14, while Article 19 deals with freedom rights.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Amendment that made education a fundamental right → 86th Amendment (2002)
☛ When was RTE Act enforced? → 1 April 2010
☛ Article 45 deals with → Education for children below 6 years (Directive Principle)
☛ Age group covered under Article 21A → 6 to 14 years
☛ Article 51A(k) imposes duty on → Parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6-14
question_hi: 6 से 14 वर्ष की आयु के बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का अधिकार किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत प्रदान किया गया है? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 1)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 51A(k)
अनुच्छेद 45
अनुच्छेद 21A
अनुच्छेद 19
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 21A

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 21A 6 से 14 वर्ष के बच्चों को निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का मौलिक अधिकार प्रदान करता है। यह अनुच्छेद 86वें संवैधानिक संशोधन (2002) के द्वारा जोड़ा गया। इस अधिकार को लागू करने के लिए बालकों का निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 (RTE Act) बनाया गया। इससे पहले अनुच्छेद 45 (अब निर्देशक सिद्धांत) में 14 वर्ष तक के बच्चों को शिक्षा का प्रावधान था, लेकिन वह मौलिक अधिकार नहीं था। अनुच्छेद 21A के तहत शिक्षा अब मौलिक अधिकार है, जो राज्य को बाध्य करता है। अनुच्छेद 51A(k) माता-पिता का कर्तव्य बताता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 19 स्वतंत्रता से संबंधित है।
